claim: cisTEM is new open-source software for the processing of data for high-resolution electron cryo-microscopy and single-particle averaging.
source: We have developed new open-source software called cisTEM (computational imaging system for transmission electron microscopy) for the processing of data for high-resolution electron cryo-microscopy and single-particle averaging.
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract as a primary contribution of the work.

claim: cisTEM features a graphical user interface that is used to submit jobs, monitor their progress, and display results.
source: cisTEM features a graphical user interface that is used to submit jobs, monitor their progress, and display results.
evidence: Directly stated description of software features.

claim: cisTEM implements a full processing pipeline including movie processing, image defocus determination, automatic particle picking, 2D classification, ab-initio 3D map generation from random parameters, 3D classification, and high-resolution refinement and reconstruction.
source: It implements a full processing pipeline including movie processing, image defocus determination, automatic particle picking, 2D classification, ab-initio 3D map generation from random parameters, 3D classification, and high-resolution refinement and reconstruction.
evidence: Directly stated description of software capabilities.

claim: Some processing steps in cisTEM implement newly-developed algorithms while others were adapted from previously published algorithms.
source: Some of these steps implement newly-developed algorithms; others were adapted from previously published algorithms.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract describing the nature of the algorithms.

claim: cisTEM is optimized to enable processing of typical datasets (2000 micrographs, 200 k – 300 k particles) on a high-end, CPU-based workstation in half a day or less.
source: The software is optimized to enable processing of typical datasets (2000 micrographs, 200 k – 300 k particles) on a high-end, CPU-based workstation in half a day or less, comparable to GPU-accelerated processing.
evidence: Directly stated performance benchmark for the software.

claim: cisTEM's processing speed is comparable to GPU-accelerated processing.
source: The software is optimized to enable processing of typical datasets (2000 micrographs, 200 k – 300 k particles) on a high-end, CPU-based workstation in half a day or less, comparable to GPU-accelerated processing.
evidence: Directly stated comparison of performance.

claim: Jobs in cisTEM can be scheduled on large computer clusters using flexible run profiles that can be adapted for most computing environments.
source: Jobs can also be scheduled on large computer clusters using flexible run profiles that can be adapted for most computing environments.
evidence: Directly stated capability of the software.

claim: cisTEM is available for download from cistem.org.
source: cisTEM is available for download from cistem.org.
evidence: Directly stated availability information.

claim: The three-dimensional (3D) visualization of biological macromolecules and their assemblies by single-particle electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) has become a prominent approach in the study of molecular mechanisms.
source: The three-dimensional (3D) visualization of biological macromolecules and their assemblies by single-particle electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) has become a prominent approach in the study of molecular mechanisms (Cheng et al., 2015; Subramaniam et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Recent advances in cryo-EM have been primarily due to the introduction of direct electron detectors.
source: Recent advances have been primarily due to the introduction of direct electron detectors (McMullan et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: With improved data quality, there is increasing demand for advanced computational algorithms to extract signal from noisy image data and reconstruct 3D density maps at the highest possible resolution.
source: With the improved data quality, there is increasing demand for advanced computational algorithms to extract signal from the noisy image data and reconstruct 3D density maps from them at the highest possible resolution.
evidence: Stated as context for the development of cisTEM.

claim: The promise of near-atomic resolution (3–4 Å) has been realized by many software tools and suites.
source: The promise of near-atomic resolution (3–4 Å), where densities can be interpreted reliably with atomic models, has been realized by many software tools and suites (Frank et al., 1996; Hohn et al., 2007; Lyumkis et al., 2013; Punjani et al., 2017; Scheres, 2012; Tang et al., 2007; van Heel et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published software tools.

claim: Many cryo-EM software tools implement a standard set of image processing steps that are now routinely performed in a single particle project.
source: Many of these tools implement a standard set of image processing steps that are now routinely performed in a single particle project.
evidence: Stated as established practice in the field.

claim: Standard cryo-EM processing steps typically include movie frame alignment, contrast transfer function (CTF) determination, particle picking, two-dimensional (2D) classification, 3D reconstruction, refinement and classification, and sharpening of the final reconstructions.
source: These typically include movie frame alignment, contrast transfer function (CTF) determination, particle picking, two-dimensional (2D) classification, 3D reconstruction, refinement and classification, and sharpening of the final reconstructions.
evidence: Stated as standard workflow in the field.

claim: cisTEM consists of a set of compiled programs and tools, as well as a wxWidgets-based GUI.
source: cisTEM consists of a set of compiled programs and tools, as well as a wxWidgets-based GUI.
evidence: Directly stated description of software architecture.

claim: The cisTEM GUI launches programs and controls them by sending specific commands and receiving results via TCP/IP sockets.
source: The GUI launches programs and controls them by sending specific commands and receiving results via TCP/IP sockets.
evidence: Directly stated description of software communication mechanism.

claim: Each cisTEM program can be run manually, in which case it solicits user input on the command line.
source: Each program can also be run manually, in which case it solicits user input on the command line.
evidence: Directly stated capability of the software.

claim: The design of cisTEM allows users who would like to have more control over the different processing steps to design their own procedures outside the GUI.
source: The design of cisTEM, therefore, allows users who would like to have more control over the different processing steps to design their own procedures outside the GUI.
evidence: Directly stated design feature of the software.

claim: A number of previously existing Fortran-based programs were rewritten in C++ for cisTEM, including Unblur and Summovie, mag_distortion_correct, CTFFIND4, and Frealign.
source: To adopt this new architecture, a number of previously existing Fortran-based programs were rewritten in C++, including Unblur and Summovie (Grant and Grigorieff, 2015b), mag_distortion_correct (Grant and Grigorieff, 2015a), CTFFIND4 (Rohou and Grigorieff, 2015), and Frealign (Lyumkis et al., 2013).
evidence: Directly stated with citations to the original programs.

claim: Algorithms for particle picking, 2D classification, and ab-initio 3D reconstruction were added to cisTEM, sometimes with modifications to optimize their performance.
source: Additionally, algorithms described previously were added for particle picking (Sigworth, 2004), 2D classification (Scheres et al., 2005) and ab-initio 3D reconstruction (Grigorieff, 2016), sometimes with modifications to optimize their performance.
evidence: Directly stated with citations to the original algorithms.

claim: cisTEM is open-source and distributed under the Janelia Research Campus Software License.
source: cisTEM is open-source and distributed under the Janelia Research Campus Software License (http://license.janelia.org/license/janelia_license_1_2.html).
evidence: Directly stated licensing information.

claim: cisTEM currently does not support computation on graphical processing units (GPUs).
source: cisTEM currently does not support computation on graphical processing units (GPUs).
evidence: Directly stated limitation of the software.

claim: An NVIDIA K40 GPU performs approximately as well as 16 Xeon E5-2687W CPU cores after the code was carefully optimized for the respective hardware in both cases.
source: Benchmarking of a hotspot identified in the global orientational search to determine particle alignment parameters showed that an NVIDIA K40 GPU performs approximately as well as 16 Xeon E5-2687W CPU cores after the code was carefully optimized for the respective hardware in both cases.
evidence: Directly stated benchmarking result.

claim: CPU code is more easily maintained and more generally compatible with existing computer hardware than GPU code.
source: Since CPU code is more easily maintained and more generally compatible with existing computer hardware, the potential benefit of GPU-adapted code is primarily the lower cost of a high-end GPU compared with a high-end CPU.
evidence: Stated as reasoning for design choice.

claim: The potential benefit of GPU-adapted code is primarily the lower cost of a high-end GPU compared with a high-end CPU.
source: Since CPU code is more easily maintained and more generally compatible with existing computer hardware, the potential benefit of GPU-adapted code is primarily the lower cost of a high-end GPU compared with a high-end CPU.
evidence: Stated as reasoning for design choice.

claim: The developers chose to focus on optimizing cisTEM code for CPUs.
source: We chose to focus on optimizing our code for CPUs.
evidence: Directly stated design decision.

claim: Movie alignment in cisTEM is based on published algorithms previously implemented in Unblur and Summovie.
source: Movie alignment and CTF determination are based on published algorithms previously implemented in Unblur and Summovie (Grant and Grigorieff, 2015b), and CTFFIND4 (Rohou and Grigorieff, 2015), respectively, and these are therefore only briefly described here.
evidence: Directly stated with citation to previous work.

claim: CTF determination in cisTEM is based on published algorithms previously implemented in CTFFIND4.
source: Movie alignment and CTF determination are based on published algorithms previously implemented in Unblur and Summovie (Grant and Grigorieff, 2015b), and CTFFIND4 (Rohou and Grigorieff, 2015), respectively, and these are therefore only briefly described here.
evidence: Directly stated with citation to previous work.

claim: Unblur determines the translations of individual movie frames necessary to bring features (particles) visible in the frames into register.
source: Unblur determines the translations of individual movie frames necessary to bring features (particles) visible in the frames into register.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm function.

claim: Each frame is aligned against a sum of all other frames that is iteratively updated until there is no further change in the translations.
source: Each frame is aligned against a sum of all other frames that is iteratively updated until there is no further change in the translations.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm procedure.

claim: The trajectories along the x- and y-axes are smoothed using a Savitzky–Golay filter to reduce the possibility of spurious translations.
source: The trajectories along the x- and y-axes are smoothed using a Savitzky–Golay filter to reduce the possibility of spurious translations.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm procedure.

claim: Summovie uses the translations to calculate a final frame average with optional exposure filtering to take into account radiation damage of protein and maximize its signal in the final average.
source: Summovie uses the translations to calculate a final frame average with optional exposure filtering to take into account radiation damage of protein and maximize its signal in the final average.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm function.

claim: cisTEM combines the functionality of Unblur and Summovie into a single panel and exposes all relevant parameters to the user.
source: cisTEM combines the functionality of Unblur and Summovie into a single panel and exposes all relevant parameters to the user (Figure 1).
evidence: Directly stated with reference to Figure 1.

claim: Both Unblur and Summovie programs were originally written in Fortran and have been rewritten entirely in C++.
source: Both programs were originally written in Fortran and have been rewritten entirely in C++.
evidence: Directly stated description of software development.

claim: CTFFIND4 fits a calculated two-dimensional CTF to Thon rings visible in the power spectrum calculated from either images or movies.
source: CTFFIND4 fits a calculated two-dimensional CTF to Thon rings (Thon, 1966) visible in the power spectrum calculated from either images or movies.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm function with citation.

claim: The fitted parameters in CTFFIND4 include astigmatism and, optionally, phase shifts generated by phase plates.
source: The fitted parameters include astigmatism and, optionally, phase shifts generated by phase plates.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm parameters.

claim: When computed from movies, the Thon rings are often more clearly visible compared to Thon rings calculated from images.
source: When computed from movies, the Thon rings are often more clearly visible compared to Thon rings calculated from images (Figure 2; [Bartesaghi et al., 2014]).
evidence: Directly stated with reference to Figure 2 and citation.

claim: An optimal value to amplify Thon rings would be to sum the number of frames that correspond to an exposure of about four electrons/Å2.
source: An optimal value to amplify Thon rings would be to sum the number of frames that correspond to an exposure of about four electrons/Å2 (McMullan et al., 2015).
evidence: Directly stated with citation to supporting literature.

claim: The initial exhaustive search over defocus values in CTFFIND4 can now be performed using a one-dimensional version of the CTF against a radial average of the amplitude spectrum.
source: (1) The initial exhaustive search over defocus values can now be performed using a one-dimensional version of the CTF (i.e. with only two parameters: defocus and phase shift) against a radial average of the amplitude spectrum.
evidence: Directly stated as a change to the algorithm.

claim: The one-dimensional CTF search is much faster than the equivalent search over the 2D CTF parameters.
source: This search is much faster than the equivalent search over the 2D CTF parameters (i.e., four parameters: two for defocus, one for astigmatism angle and one for phase shift) and can be expected to perform well except in cases of very large astigmatism (Zhang, 2016).
evidence: Directly stated with citation to supporting work.

claim: Once an initial estimate of the defocus parameter has been obtained, it is refined by a conjugate gradient minimizer against the 2D amplitude spectrum.
source: Once an initial estimate of the defocus parameter has been obtained, it is refined by a conjugate gradient minimizer against the 2D amplitude spectrum, as done previously.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm procedure.

claim: In cisTEM, the default behavior is to perform the initial search over the 1D amplitude spectrum, but the user can revert to previous behavior by setting a flag in the 'Expert Options' of the 'Find CTF' Action panel.
source: In cisTEM, the default behavior is to perform the initial search over the 1D amplitude spectrum, but the user can revert to previous behavior by setting a flag in the 'Expert Options' of the 'Find CTF' Action panel.
evidence: Directly stated description of software behavior.

claim: If the input micrograph's pixel size is smaller than 1.4 Å, the resampling and clipping of its 2D amplitude spectrum will be adjusted so as to give a final spectrum for fitting with an edge corresponding to 1/2.8 Å−1.
source: (2) If the input micrograph's pixel size is smaller than 1.4 Å, the resampling and clipping of its 2D amplitude spectrum will be adjusted so as to give a final spectrum for fitting with an edge corresponding to 1/2.8 Å−1, to avoid all of the Thon rings being located near the origin of the spectrum, where they can be very poorly sampled.
evidence: Directly stated as a change to the algorithm.

claim: Following background subtraction, a radial, sine-edged mask is applied to the spectrum, and this masked version is used during search and refinement of defocus, astigmatism and phase shift parameters.
source: (4) Following background subtraction as described in Mindell and Grigorieff (2003), a radial, sine-edged mask is applied to the spectrum, and this masked version is used during search and refinement of defocus, astigmatism and phase shift parameters.
evidence: Directly stated as a change to the algorithm with citation.

claim: The sine mask is 0.0 at the Fourier space origin, and 1.0 at a radius corresponding to 1/4 Å−1, and serves to emphasize high-resolution Thon rings.
source: The sine is 0.0 at the Fourier space origin, and 1.0 at a radius corresponding to 1/4 Å−1, and serves to emphasize high-resolution Thon rings, which are less susceptible to artefacts caused by imperfect background subtraction.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm procedure.

claim: Users receive a warning if the box size of the amplitude spectrum and the estimated defocus parameters suggest that significant CTF aliasing occurred.
source: (5) Users receive a warning if the box size of the amplitude spectrum and the estimated defocus parameters suggest that significant CTF aliasing occurred (Penczek et al., 2014).
evidence: Directly stated as a feature with citation.

claim: Putative particles are found by matching to a soft-edged disk template, which is related to a convolution with Gaussians.
source: Putative particles are found by matching to a soft-edged disk template, which is related to a convolution with Gaussians (Voss et al., 2009) but uses additional statistics based on an algorithm originally described by Sigworth (2004).
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm with citations.

claim: The use of a soft-edged disk template as opposed to structured templates greatly speeds up calculation, enabling picking in 'real time'.
source: The use of a soft-edged disk template as opposed to structured templates has two main advantages. It greatly speeds up calculation, enabling picking in 'real time', and alleviates the problem of templates biasing the result of all subsequent processing towards those templates (Henderson, 2013; Subramaniam, 2013; van Heel, 2013).
evidence: Directly stated advantage with citations.

claim: The use of a soft-edged disk template alleviates the problem of templates biasing the result of all subsequent processing towards those templates.
source: The use of a soft-edged disk template as opposed to structured templates has two main advantages. It greatly speeds up calculation, enabling picking in 'real time', and alleviates the problem of templates biasing the result of all subsequent processing towards those templates (Henderson, 2013; Subramaniam, 2013; van Heel, 2013).
evidence: Directly stated advantage with citations.

claim: Any bias introduced by the soft-edged disk template will be towards a featureless 'blob' and will likely be obvious if present.
source: Any bias that is introduced will be towards a featureless 'blob' and will likely be obvious if present.
evidence: Stated as reasoning for design choice.

claim: The user must specify three parameters for particle picking: the radius of the template disk, the maximum radius of the particle, and the detection threshold value.
source: The user must specify three parameters: the radius of the template disk, the maximum radius of the particle, which sets the minimum distance between picks, and the detection threshold value, given as a number of standard deviations of the (Gaussian) distribution of scores expected if no particles were present in the input micrograph.
evidence: Directly stated description of user input requirements.

claim: Values of 1.0 to 6.0 for the detection threshold generally give acceptable results.
source: Values of 1.0 to 6.0 for this threshold generally give acceptable results.
evidence: Directly stated guidance for parameter selection.

claim: Prior to matched filtering, micrographs are resampled by Fourier cropping to a pixel size of 15 Å.
source: Prior to matched filtering, micrographs are resampled by Fourier cropping to a pixel size of 15 Å (the user can override this by changing the 'Highest resolution used in picking' value from its default 30 Å), and then filtered with a high-pass cosine-edged aperture to remove very low-frequency density ramps caused by variations in ice thickness or uneven illumination.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm procedure.

claim: Micrographs are filtered with a high-pass cosine-edged aperture to remove very low-frequency density ramps caused by variations in ice thickness or uneven illumination.
source: Prior to matched filtering, micrographs are resampled by Fourier cropping to a pixel size of 15 Å (the user can override this by changing the 'Highest resolution used in picking' value from its default 30 Å), and then filtered with a high-pass cosine-edged aperture to remove very low-frequency density ramps caused by variations in ice thickness or uneven illumination.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm procedure.

claim: The background noise spectrum of the micrograph is estimated by computing the average rotational power spectrum of 50 areas devoid of particles.
source: The background noise spectrum of the micrograph is estimated by computing the average rotational power spectrum of 50 areas devoid of particles, and is then used to 'whiten' the background (shot +solvent) noise of the micrograph.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm procedure.

claim: When particles are very densely packed on micrographs, the background noise estimation approach can significantly over-estimate the background noise power.
source: When particles are very densely packed on micrographs, this approach can significantly over-estimate the background noise power so that users may find they have to use lower thresholds for picking.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of the algorithm.

claim: Under circumstances of densely packed particles, micrographs with much lower particle density will suffer from a higher rate of false-positive picks.
source: It might also be expected that under those circumstances, micrographs with much lower particle density will suffer from a higher rate of false-positive picks.
evidence: Stated as an expected consequence.

claim: The algorithm first computes a map of the local variance and local mean in the micrograph and the distribution of values of these mean and variance maps.
source: Our algorithm first computes a map of the local variance and local mean in the micrograph (computed over the area defined by the maximum radius given by the user [Roseman, 2004; Van Heel, 1982]) and the distribution of values of these mean and variance maps.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm procedure with citations.

claim: The average radial power spectrum of the 50 areas of the micrograph with the lowest local variance is used as an estimate of the background noise spectrum.
source: The average radial power spectrum of the 50 areas of the micrograph with the lowest local variance is then used as an estimate of the background noise spectrum.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm procedure.

claim: Matched-filter methods are susceptible to picking high-contrast features such as contaminating ice crystals or carbon films.
source: Matched-filter methods are susceptible to picking high-contrast features such as contaminating ice crystals or carbon films.
evidence: Stated as a known limitation of the method.

claim: The user can choose to ignore areas with abnormal local variance or local mean to avoid picking artifacts.
source: To avoid picking these kinds of artifacts, the user can choose to ignore areas with abnormal local variance or local mean.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm feature.

claim: Ignoring high-variance areas often helps avoid edges of problematic objects, e.g. ice crystals or carbon foils.
source: We find that ignoring high-variance areas often helps avoid edges of problematic objects, e.g. ice crystals or carbon foils, and that avoiding high- and low-mean areas helps avoid picking from areas within them, e.g. the carbon foil itself or within an ice crystal (Figure 3).
evidence: Directly stated observation with reference to Figure 3.

claim: Avoiding high- and low-mean areas helps avoid picking from areas within problematic objects.
source: We find that ignoring high-variance areas often helps avoid edges of problematic objects, e.g. ice crystals or carbon foils, and that avoiding high- and low-mean areas helps avoid picking from areas within them, e.g. the carbon foil itself or within an ice crystal (Figure 3).
evidence: Directly stated observation with reference to Figure 3.

claim: In favorable cases many erroneous picks can be avoided using the variance and mean thresholding approach.
source: We have found that in favorable cases many erroneous picks can be avoided.
evidence: Directly stated observation.

claim: Remaining false-positive picks are removed later during 2D classification.
source: Remaining false-positive picks are removed later during 2D classification.
evidence: Directly stated description of workflow.

claim: The picking algorithm can be run nearly instantaneously on a typical ~4K image, using a single processor.
source: Because of our emphasis on performance, our algorithm can be run nearly instantaneously on a typical ~4K image, using a single processor.
evidence: Directly stated performance characteristic.

claim: The Action panel presents an 'Auto preview' mode to enable interactive adjustment of the picking parameters.
source: In the Action panel, the user is presented with an 'Auto preview' mode to enable interactive adjustment of the picking parameters (Figure 3).
evidence: Directly stated description of software feature with reference to Figure 3.

claim: In Auto preview mode, the micrograph is displayed with optional and adjustable low-pass and high-pass filters, and the results of picking using the currently selected parameters are overlaid on top.
source: In this mode, the micrograph is displayed with optional and adjustable low-pass and high-pass filters, and the results of picking using the currently selected parameters are overlaid on top.
evidence: Directly stated description of software feature.

claim: Changing one or more of the parameters leads to a fast re-picking of the displayed micrograph, so that the parameters can be optimized in real-time.
source: Changing one or more of the parameters leads to a fast re-picking of the displayed micrograph, so that the parameters can be optimized in real-time.
evidence: Directly stated description of software feature.

claim: Once the three main parameters have been adjusted appropriately, the full complement of input micrographs can be picked, usually in a few seconds or minutes.
source: Once the three main parameters have been adjusted appropriately, the full complement of input micrographs can be picked, usually in a few seconds or minutes.
evidence: Directly stated performance characteristic.

claim: A single disk template would have difficulty in picking all the different types and views of particles when particles are non-uniform in size or shape.
source: A possible disadvantage of using a single disk template exists when the particles to be picked are non-uniform in size or shape (e.g. in the case of an elongated particle). In this case, it may be expected that a single template would have difficulty in picking all the different types and views of particles present, and that in this case using a number of different templates would lead to a more accurate picking.
evidence: Stated as a potential limitation.

claim: With careful optimization of the parameters, elongated particles and particles with size variation were picked adequately.
source: In practice, we found that with careful optimization of the parameters, elongated particles and particles with size variation (Figure 3) were picked adequately.
evidence: Directly stated observation with reference to Figure 3.

claim: The underlying implementation of the algorithm supports multiple references as well as reference rotation.
source: The underlying implementation of the algorithm supports multiple references as well as reference rotation.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm capability.

claim: These features may be exposed to the graphical user interface in future versions, for example enabling the use of 2D class averages as picking templates.
source: These features may be exposed to the graphical user interface in future versions, for example enabling the use of 2D class averages as picking templates (Scheres, 2015).
evidence: Stated as a future development plan with citation.

claim: 2D classification is a relatively quick and robust way to assess the quality of a single-particle dataset.
source: 2D classification is a relatively quick and robust way to assess the quality of a single-particle dataset.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: cisTEM implements a maximum likelihood algorithm for 2D classification.
source: cisTEM implements a maximum likelihood algorithm (Scheres et al., 2005) and generates fully CTF-corrected class averages that typically display clear high-resolution detail, such as secondary structure.
evidence: Directly stated with citation to the algorithm.

claim: cisTEM generates fully CTF-corrected class averages that typically display clear high-resolution detail, such as secondary structure.
source: cisTEM implements a maximum likelihood algorithm (Scheres et al., 2005) and generates fully CTF-corrected class averages that typically display clear high-resolution detail, such as secondary structure.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm output.

claim: The stepwise increase of the resolution limit and the random selection of subsets of the data reduce the chance of overfitting.
source: Apart from speeding up the calculation, the stepwise increase of the resolution limit and the random selection of subsets of the data also reduce the chance of overfitting (see also the calculation of ab-initio 3D reconstructions and 3D refinement below) and, therefore, increase the convergence radius of the 2D classification algorithm.
evidence: Directly stated reasoning for algorithm design.

claim: The noise power spectrum is calculated from the boxed particle images using the area outside the circular mask set by the user according to the expected particle size.
source: The noise power spectrum is calculated from the boxed particle images using the area outside the circular mask set by the user according to the expected particle size.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm procedure.

claim: To increase accuracy, the noise power spectrum is further averaged across 2000 randomly selected particles.
source: To increase accuracy, it is further averaged across 2000 randomly selected particles.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm procedure.

claim: The background (density outside the mask) is further normalized by adding a constant to each particle that yields a background average of zero.
source: The background (density outside the mask) is further normalized by adding a constant to each particle that yields a background average of zero.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm procedure.

claim: The refinement of 3D reconstructions in cisTEM uses a version of Frealign that was specifically designed to work with cisTEM.
source: The refinement of 3D reconstructions in cisTEM uses a version of Frealign (Lyumkis et al., 2013) that was specifically designed to work with cisTEM.
evidence: Directly stated with citation to Frealign.

claim: Most of Frealign's control parameters are exposed to the user in the 'Manual Refine' Action panel.
source: Most of Frealign's control parameters are exposed to the user in the 'Manual Refine' Action panel (Figure 4).
evidence: Directly stated with reference to Figure 4.

claim: The 'Auto Refine' and 'Ab-Initio' panels also use Frealign but manage many of the parameters automatically.
source: The 'Auto Refine' and 'Ab-Initio' panels also use Frealign but manage many of the parameters automatically (see below).
evidence: Directly stated description of software functionality.

claim: Frealign's algorithm was described previously by Grigorieff, 2007 and Lyumkis et al., 2013.
source: Frealign's algorithm was described previously (Grigorieff, 2007; Lyumkis et al., 2013) and this section will mostly cover important differences, including a new objective function used in the refinement, different particle weighting used in reconstructions, optional likelihood-based blurring, as well as new masking options.

claim: Important differences in FrealignX include a new objective function used in the refinement, different particle weighting used in reconstructions, optional likelihood-based blurring, as well as new masking options.
source: Frealign's algorithm was described previously (Grigorieff, 2007; Lyumkis et al., 2013) and this section will mostly cover important differences, including a new objective function used in the refinement, different particle weighting used in reconstructions, optional likelihood-based blurring, as well as new masking options.
evidence: Directly stated description of new features.

claim: To make Frealign compatible with cisTEM's GUI, the code was completely rewritten in C++.
source: To make Frealign compatible with cisTEM's GUI, the code was completely rewritten in C++, and it will be referred to here as Frealign v10, or FrealignX.
evidence: Directly stated description of software development.

claim: The new version makes use of a matched filter to maximize the signal in cross correlation maps calculated between particle images and reference projections.
source: The new version makes use of a matched filter (McDonough and Whalen, 1995) to maximize the signal in cross correlation maps calculated between particle images and reference projections.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm feature with citation.

claim: The matched filter requires whitening of the noise present in the images and resolution-dependent scaling of the reference projections to match the signal in the noise-whitened images.
source: This requires whitening of the noise present in the images and resolution-dependent scaling of the reference projections to match the signal in the noise-whitened images.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm requirements.

source: Both can be achieved if the spectral signal-to-noise ratio (SSNR) of the data is known.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm requirements.

claim: FrealignX can refine the defocus assigned to each particle.
source: FrealignX can refine the defocus assigned to each particle.
evidence: Directly stated description of algorithm capability.

claim: Per-particle defocus refinement may be useful when particles have a size of about 400 kDa or larger.
source: Given typical imaging conditions with current instrumentation (300 kV, direct electron detector), this may be useful when particles have a size of about 400 kDa or larger.
evidence: Stated as guidance for when to use the feature.

claim: Depending on the quality of the sample and images, large particles may generate sufficient signal to yield per-particle defocus values that are more accurate than the average defocus values determined for whole micrographs by CTFFIND4.
source: Depending on the quality of the sample and images, these particles may generate sufficient signal to yield per-particle defocus values that are more accurate than the average defocus values determined for whole micrographs by CTFFIND4 (see above).
evidence: Stated as reasoning for the feature.

source: Refinement is achieved by a simple one-dimensional grid search of a defocus offset applied to both defocus values determined in the 2D CTF fit obtained by CTFFIND4.
